notes: One iPhone 18 Pro Max on iOS 27.0.1; Release build; no screen recording performed by the suite.
Package renderer and physics match released PaperConfetti 0.2.0. Benchmark-only collection-window and startup-state fixes were required.
Five cannons per burst, 0.1-second spacing, festive shapes, 10-point nominal size, shared seeds and flight parameters. Tilt is the appearance difference.
Timing: one warm-up and two measured repetitions per mode/load, separate processes. All timing rows were nominal thermal state.
Paired CPU: one warm-up and three measured repetitions per mode/load, alternating order in the same process. CPU is whole-app time over the complete trial, not GPU time or a percentage.

Memory: six rounds per mode, alternating cancellation and natural completion; reported warm samples exclude round zero. Footprint includes app/framework caches and is not total GPU or render-server memory.
Hitches are process-attributed Animation Hitches events clipped to matching signposts, not FPS or an animation-active hitch-time ratio. Instrumentation can affect behavior.
The initial flat-180 CPU trace stalled after complete app measurements; the paired repeat successfully records that case again.
The initial 5,760-piece memory capture was polled too early and excluded. Two subsequent startup-interrupted attempts were excluded. The complete post-fix memory retry replaces them.
All 14 physical UI tests and 35 Python runner tests passed. Pixel tests cover all five cannons and all 5,760 grid slots; gesture tests cover taps, scrolling, cancellation and Reduce Motion.
Small-sample screening on one device; do not claim universal zero hitches, fixed FPS, cold-start performance, energy efficiency, or a definitive 2D/3D speed winner.

reproduction.note: Use the corrected runner. The retained paired CPU pass reused the tested Release executable; the equivalent public command rebuilds and reruns interaction checks after measuring.
